Look inside a token without verifying it

Source: R/peek.R
jose_peek.Rd

jose_peek() parses a JWS or JWE, in any serialization, and returns its headers and, for a JWS, its payload. Nothing is verified. The result is classed jose_unverified and says so when printed. Use it to decide which key or policy to apply, or to debug, never to make a decision that trusts the token. jose_verify() and jose_decrypt() are the functions that check a token.

Usage

jose_peek(token, limits = jose_limits())

Arguments

token

A token: a compact serialization, or the text of a JSON serialization.

limits

Resource limits, from jose_limits().

Value

A list of class jose_unverified with:

  • type: "JWS" or "JWE".

  • serialization: "compact", "flattened" or "general".

  • headers: one header per signature or recipient, each the union of the protected and unprotected headers.

  • payload: for a JWS, the payload as a raw vector; NULL for a JWE or a detached payload.

  • claims: the payload parsed as a list when it is a JSON object, as in a JWT; otherwise NULL.

Details

The token must still be well formed: strict unpadded Base64url, headers that are JSON objects without repeated members, and the rules on crit and b64 (RFC 7515, RFC 7797). A malformed token raises zujwt_parse_error.

Examples

token <- paste0(
  "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.",
  "eyJzdWIiOiJ1MSIsImV4cCI6MTMwMDgxOTM4MH0.",
  "c2lnbmF0dXJl"
)
jose_peek(token)
#> <jose_unverified> JWS, compact serialization
#> ! Not verified: nothing here can be trusted.
#> Header:
#>   alg: "HS256"
#>   typ: "JWT"
#> Claims:
#>   sub: "u1"
#>   exp: 1300819380
